utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Madam Court Deputy.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-01-48-T, the Prosecutor versus Sefer Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Good morning, ladies and gentlemen. Before we have the witness, are there any matters that the parties would like to bring to the attention to this Bench?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, there's one matter I could raise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: We requested yesterday of the Prosecutor if the Defence am I correct on this occasion have the opportunity to spend a period of time with the forthcoming witness for the purposes of proofing the witness, bearing in mind that he may have -- may be capable of giving some -- some theoretical and expert sort of comments, and the Prosecution were kind enough to allow us to do that, so I just indicate to the Court that that was done this morning. It was completed at about ten to 9.00, so no proofing notes of that discussion have taken place. I'm not sure that it would be required of the Defence in any event to provide proofing notes, but whether it's required or not, I've indicated to my learned friend that I put certain documents to him which I'm proposing to question him about in the future, and I thought it proper to indicate that to the Chamber. I can indicate this, that as a result of that proofing it may be - and depending upon the evidence given, as it's about to be given - it may be that I will need to take some instructions from Mr. Halilovic and also from our team member Asim Dzambasovic, who I indicate is present in court today precisely because of the -- what might be some military theory answers to be elicited from this witness. Now, I thought rather than seeking to delay the process in any way, that the -- the course best to be taken might be this: That the evidence in chief be given now and then rather than asking for a special adjournment, that just the normal break be then taken, even though it's likely to be a little bit early, and in that time I would -- I believe I would have ample time to get such instructions as I need, and then we'd be able to proceed. It's -- I had thought this witness was going to go two days. I now think it will go significantly shorter than that. It is even possible that we'll finish him today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Whenever you need time for a discussion with your client, just inform us.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, my screen isn't working -- I didn't hear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I mean that if during the proceedings you have the need to consult with your client, just do that. Inform us and we could maybe have a break, you know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: For your convenience.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. So could we have the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good morning, witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Would you please make the solemn declaration, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may sit down, please. Yes, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Good morning. Is your name Selmo Cikotic?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Yes, my name is Selmo Cikotic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And were you born on the 25th of January, 1964?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And is your occupation a retired Bosnian army officer?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you retire last year from the Bosnian federation army with the rank of brigadier but having acted as the commander of the 1st Corps for the preceding few years, which is effectively the rank of a general?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were you a career JNA officer who joined the JNA upon leaving school in 1986 and were in the JNA until May 1992, when you joined the fledgling Bosnian Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And from March 1993 to April 1994, were you the commander of an operational group called Zapad, or in English, West, which was within the 3rd Corps of the ABiH?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: From March 1993 to April 1994 I was, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And from -- when you started as the commander of the operational group or the OG Zapad, was Enver Hadzihasanovic the 3rd Corps commander and he remained in that position until about November 1993?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How many groups or how many units -- I'll put it another way. What is your understanding of what an operational group was in 1993? As briefly as you possibly can, please.

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: OGs were established as temporary units to coordinate and lead combat operations and to deal with any operational issues. The goal was to reduce the number of links towards the corps commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How many units were in the operational group under your command?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: At the moment when it was established, there were five brigades and five municipal TO staffs.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were those brigades the 307th, the 317th, the 308th, and Territorial Defence groups?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Yes, Territorial Defence units that belonged to Municipal Defence Staffs.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How many soldiers were under your command in that operational group?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: The number of soldiers varied, as did the number of units. During the summer, there were some seven to eight thousand troops who were members of the units that we have just mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Does the summer extend to September 1993?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And were you directly, as the commander of the OG Zapad, subordinated to Enver Hadzihasanovic, the 3rd Corps commander? There was no one between you and him in the chain of command.

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: That's correct

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And were you yourself based in Bugojno, where your headquarters were, that is, in -- in August, September 1993?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's where my command post was.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you have a forward command post in August and September 1993?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: I did. Close to Gornji Vakuf on Planica Mountain.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were the units under your control fighting at a front line against HVO and HV soldiers?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: At that time, we were engaged in combat with the HVO. And as for the Serbian and Montenegrin aggressor, there was not much activity on that front line.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What was the next group of ABiH soldiers not under your control which bordered your soldiers at the front line? What was the name of that unit?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: There was the Independent Prozor Battalion and also the 6th Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you know Sefer Halilovic in August and September 1993?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What position, to your understanding, did he occupy in August and September 1993?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: He was the Chief of Staff of the Supreme Command of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How did you know or how did you come to know Sefer Halilovic?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: I met him in July 1993, when I was appointed the liaison officer between the staff of the Supreme Command of the BiH army and the UNPROFOR command in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And given your position in August and September 1993 as the commander of an operational group and your experience as a career JNA and then Bosnian army officer, what was your understanding of whether or not the Chief of the Main -- the Chief of Staff of the Supreme Command could issue binding orders? Could he do so and in what circumstances?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: At the time, Rasim Delic was the commander of the General Staff. Sefer Halilovic was the Chief of Staff, the Chief of the General Staff, and my understanding is that Sefer Halilovic, in the spirit of general guidelines, orders and authorisations issued by the commander, did have the authority to issue certain orders on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: To your understanding, did he have that authority by virtue of his position or did it have to be delegated to him?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: My understanding that within the principles of work and within the general guidelines, he could do certain things. I believe that he did not have to be issued any particular orders to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What about -- what about combat orders? Were you aware whether the Chief of the Staff could issue combat orders by virtue of his position?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: My understanding is that the commander could issue orders for combat and the Chief of Staff could work on the implementation of these orders, on putting these orders to work.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you have a meeting with Sefer Halilovic in August or September 1993?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: We had a meeting. I believe that it was in late August or early September in Jablanica. The second meeting that we had was in September 1993 before the operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Just concentrate on the first meeting at the moment. Whereabouts in Jablanica was the first meeting?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: The first meeting was in Donja Jablanica at the command post of Zuka's Unit in the so-called Zuka's base.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Why did you go to a meeting with Sefer Halilovic at Zuka's base?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Because that's the order I had been issued, to go to the meeting there.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who issued you that order?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: I believe that I received this order from Sefer Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who did you go to the meeting with?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: I went with my officer for operations, Amer Durakovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who else was at the meeting?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: At the meeting, which was not very formal, there were Sefer Halilovic, Zuka, journalist [Realtime transcript read in error "General"] Sevko Hodzic, myself, and my operations officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The transcript says General Sevko Hodzic. Is that correct? The transcript, if you just look at the transcript, it says "General Sevko Hodzic." Is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: No. He was a journalist. Sevko Hodzic was a journalist.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Why did Sefer Halilovic call this meeting with you or order you to this meeting?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: At this first meeting, he announced to me that in the territory of Herzegovina there would be a combat operation taking place and that preparations should be carried out for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Which combat operation and preparations for it was he referring to?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: I am referring to something that at the time I didn't know what it was because I had not received any specific information about this operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did Sefer Halilovic tell you what the operation involved at that particular meeting?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: No. At that time, I did not have any particular information. It was only said that the operation would be undertaken in order to reduce the front line and to liberate certain roads.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: In which area?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: In the area of Herzegovina and between the municipalities of Prozor and Vakuf, closer to the borders of Bosnia, and this was all the area that I was particularly interested in.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who was to lead this particular operation?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: I understood at the time that it would be Mr. Sefer Halilovic who would be coordinating combat activities within that operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What gave you that understanding?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: I think that this is the interpretation of his words on his role: He said that he would be on the ground with a team from the General Staff and that he would be taking the coordinating role in this operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you understand that coordinating could mean issuing orders to commanders, subordinate commanders?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: I think that this did involve issuing specific orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: At that point, that first meeting, did you know what the name of the operation was?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When did you come to learn what the name of the operation was?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: I believe that I learnt it at the subsequent meeting that was held in Dobro Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What was the name?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, the name of it was Neretva 93.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How long did that first meeting last?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: The first meeting lasted for the duration of a brief lunch and coffee afterwards, so we talked over lunch.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Forgive me if I've asked you this before and you've answered it. Was Zuka present at this meeting?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Yes, he was present at the meeting. He was present during the lunch, but I actually do not recall talking about the forthcoming operation during the entire lunch.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where did you go -- I'm sorry, were you about to say something?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: I believe that Mr. Sefer Halilovic told me about the operation in his car as we were travelling to the next meeting that took place that same evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where was that next meeting?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: That meeting was in a village near Konjic. I don't -- I don't know what village that was. It was dark and the meeting took place in a military depot.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who was at the meeting?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sefer Halilovic and I met with Salko Gusic, the commander of the 6th Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What was the purpose of the meeting?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: The purpose was to inform me and Gusic who were supposed to cooperate in the forthcoming operation and to introduce us to each other, because we hadn't known each other before.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You said that Sefer Halilovic -- sorry, you travelled there in Sefer Halilovic's car. Did he -- whose idea was it for the meeting to occur?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: You're referring to that next meeting, the subsequent meeting?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That's right, the meeting with Mr. Gusic.

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: I believe that it was Mr. Sefer Halilovic's idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How long did that meeting go for?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: It was a brief meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Had you met Mr. Gusic before?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: No. That was when I saw him for the first time.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You said the purpose was to inform you and Gusic who was supposed to cooperate in the forthcoming operation. Did Mr. Halilovic discuss with you and Mr. Gusic your respective roles in the forthcoming operation?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: I don't think we were told what our specific roles were to be, but in order to act better in a coordinated action, we needed to know each other.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: On that day, did Mr. Sefer Halilovic tell you what role your OG was to perform in the operation which you came to know as Neretva?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: I don't think he told me anything specific about it that day except for telling me that my operational group was to be a participant in that operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did he want your entire operational group or merely units of it to participate in that operation?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: I think that in his view I was covering a rather wide -- a rather long front line that I had to defend and therefore I could only engage a part of my forces in this particular action, and I don't think we were at cross-purposes on that particular issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Do you remember discussing which particular forces you could offer for the operation, which of your units you could lend for the operation?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: I don't know whether we discussed the strength of our forces on this particular meeting or on some other meeting, but I believe that only one battalion was discussed as a force that could be engaged in this particular operation in addition to a reserve battalion that could be drawn upon as an optional fresh force to be used in the operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Which battalion was the one that was discussed as a force that could be engaged in that particular operation?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: We weren't talking about any specific battalions at the time. It was to be my own choice.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And did you return to your forward command post at the conclusion of this meeting?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you inform your commander, Hadzihasanovic, of the meeting and Mr. Halilovic's orders to attend the meeting?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm going to display Prosecution Exhibit P93, which is a photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: If you'd just look at the screen to your left, sir. Just look at that photograph. What is that a photograph of?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: I think that this is a photograph of Donja Jablanica. I see the house where the so-called Zuka's base was located.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Actually, someone has helpfully drawn a "1" with two arrows on it. Would that be where it is?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: In my opinion, this is the house that's been marked with the left -- or rather, the top arrow as we see it here.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown on the screen MFI192. The 65 ter number of that is 107, which we will show through Sanction. If I have to read out the ERN, it is 01814325 and 01814396. And I'll just show the witness a paper copy in Bosnian and a paper copy of the front page. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Do you recognise that, Mr. Cikotic, as an extract from a war diary of the 3rd Corps?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. That's an excerpt from the war diary of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: If the next page could please be displayed, the one that is 4396. Thank you. And if you could just enlarge the bottom half which says "OG Zapad/West." I'm sorry. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Cikotic, there's a reference there to an OG Zapad/West and at the bottom of the page the date is the 3rd or 4th of September, 1993, and at the bottom of the page a reference to you meeting the chief of the -- Chief of the Staff of the Supreme Command in Jablanica. Is it displayed in English there for you?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Do you need it in Bosnian or is the English okay?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: I think I have a printed copy of the document in Bosnian which correspond -- corresponds to the one in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: For the Court's benefit, if the Trial Chamber has read the bottom, could the next page please be shown, just the top part.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. Have you read that?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay. I'm interested in two things: Firstly, the date; and secondly, the accuracy of the details of the meeting. Is that entry referring to the meeting you had with Mr. Halilovic which you testified about over the last 20 minutes or so?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Evidently the war diary covers all the meetings that I had as I was on my way to Jablanica; namely, two. And I can see that one can read here the area on which the forces of my operational group were to be engaged within this operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. The date in the ward is the 3rd/4th of September, 1993. Do you have any reason to doubt the accuracy of that date, as to the date on which you held the meeting with Mr. Halilovic?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: The date is probably correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And are the details in that paragraph referring to the meeting more or less accurate as to the discussion you had with him?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: May that be received into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, would you please inform us about the author and the chain of custody of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It's a -- it's a war diary from the 3rd Corps, which was one of the -- the documents -- many documents the -- which came into the possession of the Office of the Prosecutor in searching the various archives. This is a 3rd Corps archive. It's called the Sarajevo collection, which I think was seized in August - I'm saying this last part from memory - August and November 2000 from the ABiH archives in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. And who is the author of this diary? Is it a personal diary or is the kind of log, you know?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It's the official 3rd Corps war diary which was kept in the operations centre and would have been written by the operations officer on the staff of the commander of the 3rd Corps. As far as we can -- we can ascertain, it is just a standard war diary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Any objections, Mr. Morrissey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, with respect to this specific war diary and given the answers that the witness has already given, we don't seek to press any further issues with it. We agree that in this case -- I'm deal with them on a case-by-case basis, but in this case it should be permitted to be admitted into the evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. It is admitted into the evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be Prosecution Exhibit P192.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Cikotic, when did you next meet Sefer Halilovic?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: The next time I met Mr. Sefer Halilovic, at Dobro Polje, several days prior to the operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How long after the first meeting, which having looked at the war diary you agree was probably on the 3rd or 4th of September, 1993 -- how long after that was it?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Several days later.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Whereabouts at Dobro Polje did you meet?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: We met at the command of the Independent Prozor Battalion, commanded by Enver Buza.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Why did you go there?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Because I received an order to attend the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: From whom?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: From Mr. Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was your commander of the 3rd Corps, Hadzihasanovic, aware that you -- that Mr. Halilovic had ordered you to attend the meeting at the -- that meeting?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Yes. I informed my commander of the earlier meetings and got his consent for my participation in the operation to take part in the region of Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who was at the meeting? Was there anyone from the General Staff?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: In addition to Mr. Sefer Halilovic, there was Mr. Suljevic, Rifat Bilajac, and Vehbija Karic from the Main -- the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was there anyone from the 6th Corps there?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: There was the commander of the 6th Corps, and I recall the brigade commanders, Haso Hakalovic, Enes Kovacovic, and the commander of the Prozor Battalion, Buza.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The commander of the 6th Corps, that -- you're referring to Mr. Gusic there?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What about the 4th Corps -- the 4th Corps?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: I don't remember seeing anyone from the 4th Corps there, unless some of the brigades present -- or rather, the commanders present there were from the 4th Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who came from your operational group?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: With me, there were my officers for operational and intelligence affairs, Kenan Dautovic and Tahir Granic and Enver Zejnilagic.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter missed the name of one of the first two assistants.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Would you just repeat the first name. Kenan Dautovic. There was someone else you mentioned.

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Amir Durakovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What was Tahir Granic's position?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Tahir Granic was commander of the 307th Motorised Brigade from Bugojno at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What about Enver Zejnilagic? What was his position?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Enver Zejnilagic was commander of the 317th Brigade from Gornji Vakuf.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: About how many people in total were at this meeting?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: I think there were some 10 to 15 people in the room where we had the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who was chairing or running the meeting?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: The meeting was chaired by Mr. Sefer Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What was the purpose of the meeting?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: The purpose of the meeting was to issue specific tasks for the operation to the units participating in it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You said the meeting was chaired by Mr. Halilovic. Who was in charge of the operation?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: As concerned my own position, my understanding was that the operation was led and, had been earlier told to me, coordinated by Mr. Sefer Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did Mr. Halilovic issue orders to the various units at that meeting as to their roles in this operation?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Yes, he did specify the unit's tasks within the operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What task did he specify for you and your units?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: The task for my operational group was to launch an attack from the village of Planjiste and to seize --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The location the interpreter missed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you just repeat that last location you were to seize, please.

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: To launch an attack from the area of Voljice and Planjiste to seize the area of Vilica Guvno.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Which of your units were to do this?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: In this particular attack, the -- a battalion of the 307th Motorised Brigade took place, which was reinforced to a certain extent by the forces from the Territorial Defence Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was the 3rd Corps command to have any role at all in this particular operation that Mr. Halilovic -- in which Mr. Halilovic was issuing orders?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: It was my understanding that the 3rd Corps wasn't in any way tasked to do so, but I did perceive my unit as still forming part of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was your unit or were you receiving orders from the 3rd Corps in relation to this operation or were you only receiving them from Mr. Halilovic?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: In relation to this operation, my orders came directly from Mr. Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did Mr. Halilovic also give orders to 6th Corps units at that meeting as to their role in the operation?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What did he tell them their role was to be?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: As far as I remember, the main task of the 6th Corps was to capture the area of Crni Vrh and Makljen.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What about the Prozor Independent Battalion?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: In my understanding, the battalion was involved in this task. The 6th Corps may have had some obligations to the south as well, but for me the task related to Crni Vrh and Makljen was interesting about it affected in a way the manner in which I was to carry out my orders, my task.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did Mr. Halilovic give Buza, Enver Buza, any orders in relation to his unit at that meeting, what it was to do?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: I think that Enver Buza was also given his task at this meeting by Mr. Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Do you remember what that task was?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: I don't remember. I think that the task was one that came under the general task of -- given to the 6th Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was Zuka at this -- at this second meeting you had with Mr. Halilovic?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What was his unit called?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: His unit was called the Unit of the General Staff for Special Purposes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who was it subordinated -- or who was he subordinated to?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: In my understanding, he was subordinated to the General Staff, to the commander of the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I want you to have a look at the large map just behind you to the right, headed -- headed "Operacija Neretva." That is Exhibit D131. When did you first see that map, Mr. Cikotic? Do you remember if you saw it at that meeting, the second meeting we've just been talking about?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Yes. I believe this is the map that was presented at this meeting, where we -- where we received specific tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who presented the map?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: I believe the map was attended there, that Mr. Suljevic and Bilajac commented on their tasks by drawing upon the map. And I'm referring to the tasks assigned by Mr. Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Are you saying that people at the map [sic] drew on the map, put the map together at that particular meeting? Or are you saying they drew over it? What are you saying?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: We had a map at the meeting that had already been drawn out, so that they were merely pointing to the map and explaining the specifics of the tasks assigned to different units by pointing to different locations on the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And are the specific assignments given to your unit, that is, the OG Zapad, on that map? Just watch those headphones.

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Yes. The map does show the task assigned to my operational group.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Perhaps if you could just get the pointer and for the -- for the Trial Chamber point to where those specific assignments are marked on the map.

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. You're pointing to the area in which OG Zapad is marked.

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: [No audible response]

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You'll have to speak into the microphone.

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: I've just shown the area where the Operational Group West was supposed to carry out its attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And you're pointing down the line, pointing south, circling it.

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Now, just go to the right, and you'll see marked on the map "317th Brigade." Was that the unit you were referring to before which was a unit of your OG?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Why is that marked separately on the map to "OG Zapad"?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Because the area of responsibility of the OG West was much broader. And the map only shows the task that the operational group was supposed to carry out, that is, the area where the operational group was supposed to launch its attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What I want to just concentrate on at the moment is the difference between OG Zapad and the 317th. You told us -- the Trial Chamber earlier that the 317th was a unit within OG Zapad. Now, here on the map, "OG Zapad" is marked in a different area to the 317th. Does that mean else that the 317th was operating outside the OG Zapad or does it mean something? I'm talking only for the purposes of Operation Neretva.

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: It wasn't my understanding that the 317th was acting outside the OG, but my understanding was that the 317th was given an assignment to launch an attack. In my understanding, the 317th was defending the area within its responsibility; whereas, the units of the OG West were to launch an attack along a different axis that I've just pointed out here.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Do you mean by that that the 317th was already in that particular area when the map was drawn up?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: The 317th Brigade was here as well as here, so this was the total area of responsibility of the 317th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Just -- just for the record, you were marking down the blue line which is in the middle -- on the top of the map, from the top to where it says "317th."

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can I just clarify that? Are you saying by that the 317th was already precisely in that area?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Have a look at the map and you'll see two names. At the bottom, you'll see Sefer Halilovic's name and at the top you'll see Rasim Delic's name. What -- what is the significance of Sefer Halilovic's name being at the bottom of the map? What does that mean? The bottom right-hand corner.

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: It is my understanding that Mr. Halilovic signed the map as the leader of the team who had drawn up the map in the first place, and it is also my understanding that the commander, Mr. Rasim Delic, signed the map as the commander of the Supreme Staff and that in this way he approved the operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Under JNA or ABiH doctrine, did the -- was the person leading the operation, that is, the person commanding the operation, required to sign such a map?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: I believe that there were several options as to who signed such maps; however, in this particular situation, the map was signed in the way I've just explained to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And did your units in fact go into battle in accordance with the plans and orders drawn up at that meeting at Dobro Polje?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Approximately when?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: I saw documents that mentioned the 13th; however, I remember that it was sometime in mid-September.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How did you receive the order to act in accordance with that plan and that map?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: I received verbal orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who were the orders from?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: From Mr. Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did he personally convey them to you or did they come through someone else?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: He did it personally, directly, at the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What about the actual attack itself? Did he give you an order before or on the day of the attack to participate in it?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: I believe that on the day when the operation started we received a signal of some sort. I believe that it was a coded signal that meant the operation has started, that the attack was to be launched.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who was that from?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Also from Mr. Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How long did you and your group participate - that's OG Zapad - participate in this operation for?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: During the first day of attack, I reached Vilica Guvno.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How many days were you involved in this operation, that is, after you received the -- a signal that the operation had started?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: I sent reports to Sefer Halilovic for the next few days, and it was my understanding that this is -- this was the duration of the operation. However, my troops remained in the area even after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You were sending reports to Sefer Halilovic. Were you receiving orders from Sefer Halilovic in relation to your group's participation in that operation over those few days?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: I don't remember having received any further orders on the engagement of my OG after that meeting. It was my standing order to perform the tasks that I had been given and that was all.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How long was your OG participating in that operation?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: I remember that I had communication with Mr. Sefer Halilovic and members of his team for a few days; however, my OG continued engaging in combat even after that in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When did your communication with Mr. Halilovic cease in relation to your combat role in that area?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: A couple of days after the launch of the operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you consider your -- I'm sorry, I withdraw that. And to be completely clear about this, during those few days was your OG subordinated to Enver Hadzihasanovic, as the 3rd Corps commander, or Sefer Halilovic in this operation, just for those few days?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: I was still on the strength of the 3rd Corps; however, I was temporarily engaged in the operation that was coordinated by Mr. Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: To clarify that, do you mean that you were -- your group was subordinated to Sefer Halilovic for those few days?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: I don't remember having received an order resubordinating me to him. However, I did receive an order and approval to participate in the operation that was coordinated by him.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were you -- were you reporting back to your commander - that's Enver Hadzihasanovic - during those few days as to what your group was doing?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Yes. I sent my combat reports to him as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Could the witness -- I want to show him MFI -- I'm sorry, MFI124, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: This is an order dated -- or a document headed "Order," dated the 15th of September, 1993 and signed by Sefer Halilovic. Can you see it in front of you on the screen in it should be there in Bosnian for you.

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Can this be zoomed in a little? It is quite illegible as it is now.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'll give you a hard copy, if it might assist.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, since the witness has a hard copy, could we have the English version on our screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can we show it through Sanction? It might be a little bit quicker.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can Your Honours see it now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Do Your Honours wish to see the second page of the order now? We can broadcast that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Cikotic, do you remember seeing that order -- did you ever see that order in -- in September 1993?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: No. Today is the first time I see this order.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When you say "today," do you mean when you came to The Hague, as opposed to this morning in court?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: I didn't say "today." I said "here." -- Here I see this order for the first time.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I just want you to comment on the meaning of this order. It's signed by Sefer Halilovic and is directed to one of your -- a brigade which was under your command, the 317th. What does that mean to you as the commander of OG Zapad to which the 317th was subordinated? What -- I mean, what does this order mean in military terms, an order from Sefer Halilovic directed to the commander of a subordinate unit of yours?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: In principle, the orders issued to my unit would be via my command or via myself; however, I deem that the situation on the ground, the distance between the command post, and the inability to communicate dictated certain solutions when it came to issuing orders to the units that were on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was it a normal or an unusual situation for the -- a commander in Sefer Halilovic's position to be issuing this sort of order, an order with that detail in it to the subordinate commanders of the -- to subordinate commanders of units such as the 317th, the 45th, and the Prozor Independent Battalion?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: This was not a common way to issue orders, but it was a possibility. And within this possibility, I don't see it strange to issue specific orders to the units that were engaged in certain tasks in this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Is that order consistent with the markings on the map, which is Exhibit D131, behind you where "OG Zapad" is marked separately on the map to the "317th Brigade"?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Yes. The units were engaged in those areas where they had been engaged in combat before that, or in other words, in the area where they were supposed to be when they had been given their tasks in Dobro Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I want you to have a look at, please, another document, which is MFI193, which is Prosecution 65 ter exhibit number L0107043, B/C/S 03342945, and we'll do that via Sanction in English and I will show you -- give you a hard copy in Bosnian to read. For the record, it's a document dated the 15th of September, 1993 headed "Command for attack," and is signed by Enver Zejnilagic, the commander of the 317th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Could I just -- we are doing this one through -- we are broadcasting this one through Sanction. It's a multiple-page document. One, two, three, four -- a six-page document. So perhaps if Your Honours could signal to us, we'll -- we'll -- signal to the case manager, she'll move the pages one by one for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Sorry, just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, could I just clarify something here. We think this is already in evidence as MFI151 -- 150, I'm sorry. I just want to make sure that we're -- because we've cross-examined other witnesses about it, I think. We just want to make sure that we're not doubling up on the exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Which of course is going to happen from time to time, but I think this is one that we've already put into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Is the same document?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Just checking, Your Honour. 150 or 151?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: 150 I'm instructed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes, I've been completely correct and I apologise. It is in fact -- it's MFI150.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Cikotic, having looked at that document which purports to be an order from the commander of the 317th, I want you to comment upon it in relation to the document you just saw which was an order from Mr. Halilovic directed to that very brigade. Firstly, have you seen that document before -- that document before coming to The Hague?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: No. The first time I've seen this document was here. And I believe that this combat command for attack is a typical example of a complete order for attack, and this is the implementation of the task given by Mr. Sefer Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And that implementation, is that, too, consistent with the markings on that map which give the 317th a different area to OG Zapad? I'm referring to map D131, Operation Neretva.

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: This task is linked with the area of responsibility where the 2nd Battalion of the 317th Brigade was. In other words, this task that the 317th received, although this links up with the Independent Battalion Prozor, the task refers to the units which are here and which carry out the task in the areas previously assigned to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: While your units were engaged in Operation Neretva, did you at that time hear of -- about the killings of any Croat civilians in Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: [interpretation inaudible]

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I think you said no. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: That is correct. I didn't hear.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When did you first hear about that?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: I believe that I heard about Grabovica after the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What about Uzdol? Did you hear that Croat civilians had died during the attack on Uzdol?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: I heard that a few days after the operation on one of the local Croatian radio stations.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That's the evidence in chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, we might have a longer break and we'll resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Your cross-examination, Mr. Morrissey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And thank you very much, Mr. Cikotic. Could I just start the questions by asking you this: You knew Sefer Halilovic before you took up your position in Central Bosnia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And you -- it doesn't matter what it was now, but you had a job in Sarajevo up until late in 1992; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. And after that, you performed a number of different functions in the area of the 3rd Corps, ultimately becoming commander of Operations Group Zapad; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And ultimately -- and during that time, you dealt with Sefer Halilovic on a professional basis relatively frequently; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Yes. In the period between July and October, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. And in the time that you knew Sefer Halilovic right up to the time of this operation, frankly, what attitude did Sefer Halilovic express to you about the treatment of civilians by the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: In this respect, Sefer Halilovic left the impression also to me of a honourable officer who adhered to the customs and laws of war.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And as far as you understood the policies of the Bosnian army and indeed the Bosnian state generally at that time, was it your policy to fight for and maintain a multi-ethnic Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Yes. That was also the official policy, and as it seems to me, the personal belief of most of the people who were in the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. And included in that number of persons, to your observation, was Sefer Halilovic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: I think he was at the forefront in that respect.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And to your knowledge, was it Sefer Halilovic who led the way in introducing the rules in the Bosnian army governing the application of the Geneva Conventions late in 1992?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: I think that this took place precisely at the time when he was at the head of the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. And to your knowledge, was it Sefer Halilovic who led the attempts to bring the armed forces in Bosnia into the shape of a regular and accountable army?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Yes. I think that throughout his office at the head of the staff he was working along those lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Now, I've got some questions about the effect on the Bosnian army's efforts of any atrocities against civilians. Given the policies of the army and the Bosnian government to encourage a multi-ethnic Bosnia, is it the fact that killings of civilians or indeed any mistreatment of civilians was completely contrary to the successful implementation of the Bosnian army's policy?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Yes, that was not in accordance with the policy and principles of strengthening the Bosnian army.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Just to use your experience as an example, did you have to deal from time to time with angry and upset civilians who had been displaced from their homes in your area of combat?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did have such an experience.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And did you in those situations advise them in the best way that you could that pursuing a policy of revenge was very counter-productive and dangerous for the war effort?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. Is it also the case that -- I think I've asked you enough questions about that. Thank you. Mr. Cikotic, I'm going to ask you some questions -- questions in this cross-examination really of two types: One, they're going to be narrative questions about the facts of what happened; and there will also be some questions concerning various aspects of military doctrine and details of that nature. The questions, I have to say, will be mixed in together to some degree, but feel free to ask for clarification of any question you wish and to stop me if you think the questions are proceeding misleadingly or too fast in any form. My first question relates to a topic raised by the Prosecutor, and that is: What is an operations group? And I've got some questions about the nature of an operations group. Now, firstly, is an operations group a temporary formation within the army structure?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: In principle, it is a temporary formation, but the operations group that I commanded over was in existence for a bit over one year.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Apart from tactical groups -- well, perhaps I'll ask you another question. Are there three types of such temporary -- or were there three types of such temporary structures within the Bosnian army at that time: Tactical groups, which were quite small in nature; operations groups, which were at a level above the brigade but below the corps; and at the top level, the possibility of a strategic group? And perhaps I should ask the question now that I've listed those -- those topics. In principle, is there the possibility within the army of creating groups at those three levels, tactical group, operations group, and strategic group?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Now, dealing with the -- with the -- with an operations group. Is an operations group a group that exists above the level of a brigade but below the level of a corps?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. And is the person appointed to command an operations group generally speaking someone who is, one might say, a particularly competent person at the brigade level? In other words, it might -- it would be appropriate to appoint a person of the seniority of a brigade commander and, in addition, someone who is pretty good.

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. One thing that you never heard at the time or now is that Sefer Halilovic had been appointed as commander of an operations group; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And as far as you're concerned, whatever may have happened down in the Neretva Valley in September 1993, Sefer Halilovic wasn't the commander of an operations group, as far as you're concerned. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And indeed, appointing someone of Sefer Halilovic's seniority to a position in charge of one of these temporary formations, an operations group or even a strategic group, would have required a presidential order; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Probably. Perhaps the commander of the General Staff also had the authority to set up such a temporary formation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. And I'm going to come to the -- the powers of the commander of the General Staff in a moment. But when you refer to the commander of the General Staff, at all times in the relevant period that person was Commander Rasim Delic, whose name appears on the map to your right; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: [No audible response]

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I don't think the interpreter caught your answer to that question.

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Now, you were -- perhaps I've just got a couple of other questions about temporary formations to ask you. In creating a temporary formation such as an operations group, it is very, very important that the order creating that group specify who the commander is and which units are to be under that commander's control in order to avoid confusion with other permanent organic groups in the area. Is that an accurate statement by me?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. And in addition, I believe that the order will specify the tasks of both the commander and the operations group.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Would you just excuse me one moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Could the witness please be now shown on the computer Defence document D41. It's MFI, marked for Exhibit at the moment, 144.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Mr. Cikotic on the screen in a moment the document is going to be shown. I'm sorry. Do you have before you the Bosnian version of that at this stage?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: At the moment, I have the English version on the screen. But for a moment there I had the Bosnian version as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: So did I. There are technical hitches from time to time here. Would you just bear with us, please, for a moment. Now, you have it now?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, this is -- this is not an order that concerns you directly. I'm just asking you to comment on it as an example of an order and -- and the information provided in it. Now, does that appear to you to be a decision creating a temporary command named JUG?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And at paragraph 2, does it spell out a method by which the organisation and establishment structure of JUG may be established?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's what item 2 says.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. Could the witness please be shown the following page which is attached to this decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Do you have in front of you now another document appointing particular people to particular functions within that operations -- in that temporary command of JUG -- of the JUG group?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And without going through each of the -- each of the officeholders in that -- in that group, it specifies a commander and it specifies particular members of the staff and their functions; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And it's created by the president of the republic of the Bosnian Presidency, Alija Izetbegovic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And -- very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I just ask that the witness be shown one more such document, and this is D287. Now, Your Honours, this is only just being brought into being now. It has not yet been uploaded. We have copies which has now be distributed. What you have, Your Honours, is both the English and Bosnian stapled together. And could the Prosecutors please be provided with a copy of that as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Mr. Cikotic, could I indicate to the Court as well that we will very speedily provide this and have it scanned and loaded into the system of documents. The English version -- sorry, the front two pages ought to be in Bosnian. Do you have those?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Does this appear to be an order creating an operations group on Igman?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And does this order also specify the -- the units to be included in that -- in that group in paragraph number 2 at A and B?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Importantly, under -- under B, the 6th Corps -- does it indicate that to be taken from the 6th Corps is the special -- the Special Zulfikar Detachment for special purposes and then giving a detail, VJ military unit 5683.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Yes, it does. It's included in the list as a unit on the strength of the 6th Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. I'm just going to ask you a question -- I'm going to go through more questions on this document in a moment, but I'd just ask you about the Zulfikar unit. Although the Zulfikar unit is here in this order recognised to be part of the 6th Corps, was it your understanding that the -- the Zulfikar unit always signed itself as being a special detachment of the General Staff?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's how I remember the title and the position of the unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Was it the case that at that stage the system of command and control in the -- in the Bosnian army whilst the leadership were attempting to get it to work, not all the units operated efficiently within that system of command and control and, in particular, I would ask you if -- well, I'll ask you that general question first and then I'll ask you about the Zulfikar unit after that? I think if the question is woolly, which I recognise it is, I shall withdraw it and I'll ask a more focussed question. At that time, did it sometimes happen that units would be apparently under the command of one organic structure, such as a corps, and would occasionally comply with that but otherwise represent themselves to be accountable only -- to some other higher unit?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Would you please clarify a bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did it ever happen that a unit was supposed to be subordinated to a corps command but in fact acted as if it was subordinated to someone else? For example, the General Staff or a different corps.

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: I believe that such examples could be found, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Did you have direct experience of that yourself in your own area, or is it just something that you heard about in other areas?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: In some instances that I experienced, the status of a certain unit would not really be clear. In such cases, however, I sought clarifications.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. And could I just ask you now -- I'm going to come to this in detail later, but as to the status of the 317th Brigade about which the Prosecutor asked you some questions, was there late in August of 1993 some doubts as to the -- to where that unit, the 317th, was assigned, your unit or the 6th Corps?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: At the time, it was very clear to me that this unit belonged to my operations group.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. In this case, we've had evidence from a commander called Salko Gusic, the commander of the 6th Corps. And when he was asked to list the relevant units in -- that were under the 6th Corps, he told this Tribunal that among those units was the 317th Brigade. Now, I understand what you say, that you're quite clear that it was under your command, and I just ask you to comment upon that. Do you know -- and you may not know, but if you do know, could you explain: Do you know how it is that Commander Gusic could come to that conclusion, that the 317th was under his command?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: I think it was in early summer. I'm not sure exactly when the 6th Corps was established, but with the formation of the corps, the 317th Brigade entered -- formed part of the 6th Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: However, the situation on the ground dictated a more practical status of the unit vis-a-vis the operations group, and that's -- that was the prevailing mood in the brigade anyhow, and it seems to me that I received an interpretation from the 3rd Corps that the 317th Brigade was to remain on the strength, and that is, to remain part of the operations group. And that's how I understood it to be within my operations group.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. I understand that. And perhaps just to conclude that, you had a good working relationship too, did you not, with Enver Zejnilagic, who was the commander of that brigade at the time?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Well, I'm going to come back to that a bit later at an appropriate moment. At the moment, I was just getting you to notice some things about this order. At paragraph -- would you mind just turning over the page to the following page. And just note that this temporary formation was directly subordinated to the 1st Corps command. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Do you see paragraph 3 of the order?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Well, could I just ask you this: It's very important in creating temporary functions to make it quite clear who those -- let me start that again. I'm sorry. It's very important when creating a temporary formation that it be specified who that formation answers to and is accountable to; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: [No audible response]

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And for those who are not military people here, the reasoning behind all of this really is to protect the principle of single command so that orders are carried out in a coherent and meaningful fashion in the armed forces; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Cikotic. The -- the interpretation here did not pick up your answer to a question a little bit of a minute ago, so I'm going to ask you that question again just so that the answer can be recorded. This is at page 40, line 16, Your Honours. And the question was this -- in fact, it's at line 18. Question: "It's very important when creating a temporary formation that it be specified who that formation answers to and is accountable to; is that correct?" And that was my question. What's the answer?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you. Very well. And in short, the order that you've just seen here is an appropriate, adequate, and sensible order by which to create a temporary military formation, as far as you can see; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. I offer that document for tender. It should be marked as MFI193.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Notwithstanding there's been no explanation as to the provenance of the document, the Prosecution isn't objecting to its tender.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Morrissey, would you please inform us about the source and the chain of custody of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: It's got an ERN number. It's a Prosecution document. 01850231. So provided to us by the Prosecutors.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you very much. So this document is admitted into the evidence. And what's the MFI document on it?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This document will be Defence Exhibit D193.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And perhaps the final question about operations groups is: It's absolutely crucial that the order creating the operations group spell out who the commander is; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, the next area of military doctrine that we move to is the nature of forward command posts, also known in this Tribunal as IKMs. Now, an IKM, a forward command post, to your knowledge is a kind of -- is one of a variety of derivative command posts, which includes forward command posts, rear command posts, and a number of other kinds of temporary command posts. Is that correct generally speaking?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: It's axiomatic, is it not, that in each case where there's a forward command post there really have to be a command post.

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: A forward command post can be staffed by -- perhaps I'll withdraw that. To your knowledge, there was a forward command post of the General Staff positioned in the town of Zenica during the course of 1993? Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: I don't know whether it was in Zenica or in Kakanj. It -- yes, maybe it was in Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Very well. I'm just going to ask you to look at the order creating that document for your comments.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown -- this is MFI135, a document which is, I think --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour. Might I just raise one matter. Your Honour, you'll recall that many documents were introduced through the witness Mr. Gusic a long time ago, and at that time submissions were called for regarding the admissibility of evidence tendered by the Prosecutor and the Defence. The Prosecution indicated at that time that they had no objection to any of those documents going in, but Your Honours have not yet ruled on that because the Defence objected to a limited number of those documents for a variety of reasons. As expressed in due course this Tribunal will rule. For that reason, I'll continue to refer to the -- the Defence ones as "MFI" because they haven't been ruled upon yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you. Sorry, Mr. Cikotic. Very well. Now, do you have in front of you now a document that's -- in the Bosnian language it creates a forward command post in Zenica?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Yes, I have it, but it is rather illegible.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Well, if -- if you need to clarify any particular part, there's an English translation of it admitted, but I'll just take you through some of the details. Does this appear to be a typical order creating a -- a forward command post, an IKM? Or perhaps I should ask you: Do you need that to be enlarged, what you have in front of you now?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could the witness please have that enlarged for him.

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: I can see the document now, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Good. Now, I just want you to comment on a couple characteristics of -- of IKMs generally, and in particular by reference to this order. Firstly, in -- in analysing that order, is it fact that no person is individually specified as being the commander of that IKM, and the reason being that -- sorry, yes, well, first of all I just ask you to confirm that. But there -- there is no commander of the IKM specified as such in that order?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: I can -- I cannot see it in this order.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. But nevertheless, a number of persons are designated to perform particular functions at that IKM; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, is it also the fact that this IKM in Zenica and IKMs in general can perfectly well continue to function without there being any commander present at all but just have staff there doing their information-collecting and the other sort of tasks that they perform?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: I don't think it was possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: For example, just -- just considering this IKM that's listed here: Supposing on a particular day there had have been present the IKM, the people listed on that list, numbers 3, 4, and 5 and nobody else was present. Just -- and this is only an example.

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: In such a situation, none of those people would be the commander of any combat operations just merely by virtue of being at the IKM on that day; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: It is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. And I think rather than -- I don't want to beat around the bush about this. I'll put the -- the specific proposition that I want to put in the end so that everyone understands where it's going. Just because there's an IKM in existence doesn't mean that any operation is being commanded from it at that particular time; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: It is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. I've got another question now. I'm not sure if you're aware of this or not, Mr. Cikotic, but in this case there was said to be an IKM in Jablanica, and in fact it was referred to in -- in -- from time to time by -- by various people. Did you ever see an IKM as you would understand a real proper IKM to be in Jablanica when you were there?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Are you referring to the IKM of the General Staff?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
