utterances.text: That's what I'm referring to.

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And if an IKM was established in order to deal with an operation of the size of Neretva 93, you would expect to see an IKM with proper communications; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: With proper military police to protect and provide security for that command post; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Either a military police unit or any other unit providing security.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. And the various branches appropriate to the conduct of an operation like this, such as a chief of artillery and the other branches that one would normally find; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: You've heard of such a thing as an inspection team before, haven't you?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: I heard that term, but not during the operation. I believe that I heard it somewhat later.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Later on were you asked by -- by any lawyers or by any people at all here in The Hague to comment upon an order dated the 30th of August, 1993 that set up an inspection team and made Sefer Halilovic the head of it?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Yes. I saw that order during the preparations, and to a certain extent I provided my comment to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. I'm going to ask you for your comment about that later. At this stage, I'm just asking you really about the -- an inspection team. And I wanted to ask you this question: Is there an official name that you know of for the place where an inspection team bases itself when it's out in the terrain? Is there some official terminology for that place?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Not that I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Well, if it -- if an inspection team was to refer to its officers in shorthand as an "IKM"," would that seem to you to be a lazy but comprehensible mistake to make, given what you know about --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The Prosecution objects to the inherent speculation in that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, maybe it's a mischaracterisation, you know. Unless -- unless you have some -- some evidence, you know, to show how it is called.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this stage the admissibility of -- of the -- of some of the documents using that term has not been determined by the Tribunal yet, so I don't want to descend to the particulars of those documents. But it may be the case in the future that the Tribunal has to deal with the use of the term "IKM" by certain people. And what I want to do is to -- what I'm seeking here and I want the witness to understand precisely -- I don't want to make a speech about it, however. I'll put it as carefully as I can. I want to test how it is that that term could be used. If somebody says "IKM," does it really mean they're referring to an official IKM or might it be shorthand for something else? That's really the issue that I wanted to test with this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You may differentiate the nature of the IKM with the inspection team, you know, what's the difference between the two, you know, how it is used normally, you know. You may ask some questions along this line.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, as the Court pleases.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Cikotic, having been given some guidance, I'll ask you -- ask you those questions. Normally speaking, there's no term that you know of for the base of an inspection team; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: I don't know, because the inspection team is usually accepted by the unit which is the subject of this inspection and the inspection team stays with the unit throughout the course of the inspection.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. The evidence in this case is that the order setting up the inspection team didn't limit its job just to one corps but required it to coordinate between the 4th Corps and the 6th Corps, so that it didn't have a -- an inherent place that it had to go to in the way you've described. But following from that, normally speaking an IKM is -- is a institution that -- from which a commander can issue commands when he's on the field; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: It is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: So if a commander comes to the IKM, he's able to issue commands from that spot.

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: But I believe so also possible, isn't it, that a person might use the term "IKM" wrongly and lazily, but as shorthand, simply to describe the resting place of the -- of the inspection team? Do you agree with that possibility?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: I can't rule this out, but I don't think that this would be done by a good soldier.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Because it would be a lazy use of terminology; correct?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Yes, one might interpret it this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Thanks. Okay. Now, I just want to take you now to some narrative matters. You were not present at the meeting of corps commanders in Zenica on the 21st and 22nd of August, 1993; is that true?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: However, even before that time, troops in the area of your responsibility had been contemplating attacks along the very lines which are indicated on the map to your right, Operation Neretva; is that true?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: [No audible response]

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'm sorry. The interpreter didn't pick up your answer there. Would you mind answering again, please.

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: That is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And in fact when you came to make the attacks that you did ultimately make, they proceeded very much along the lines which you had already considered in the time before the Zenica meeting took place; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: We took the most logical axes of attack. They had been considered previously and they were included in this mission.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. And indeed --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could the witness just be shown -- yes, sorry. This -- we have another new document here which has not been uploaded yet. Copy wills be now provided to everyone. This is -- I'm going to show an order which -- I'll get you to consider whether it's yours or not, but it seems to be yours, dated 30th of July, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And would you mind just inspecting that document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And Your Honours and Mr. Prosecutor, could I just indicate that the provenance of this document that's being shown to the witness now is one that was collected by our inspector -- our team member Mr. Dzambasovic in the archives of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina during one of his two visits between 2002 to 2005 to those archives. There were ten such visits that he made there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Do you recognise that order?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: It looks logical to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And in effect, does it indicate that you were actively engaged in combat activities at that time in that area?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, I offer that document for tender, and it should be marked as MFI194.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: No, so long as the witness indicates that it is in fact his order. It wasn't quite clear from the last -- the answer was "it looks logical to me," rather than "that was an order that I signed." If the witness indicates that, we don't object it to.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, certainly, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I understand that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Is the document you have in front of you signed by you?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure, but it is logical and it is very possible that I signed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. Well, the document that you have not bearing your signature, what do you say about that document? Do you say that is an order from you on that date or not?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: It is possible that I issued a verbal order to that effect and that my assistant for intelligence turned into -- turned that into a written order and sent this order via our communication means, and I can tell that it was my assistant by the initials.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. I understand what you say. So is your position this: That you certainly issued an order to that effect, whether you produced that written order or somebody else did. You're not sure? Is that an accurate way to put the position?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Well, yes, I'd persist for the tender.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, it's admitted into the evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This document will be Defence Exhibit D194.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, at some stage early in September you were requested to go for a meeting with Sefer Halilovic in Jablanica. Can I ask you whether that was an order given to you personally by Sefer Halilovic or was it an order that came through the 3rd Corps command.

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: This order may have arrived via the 3rd Corps or maybe via the command of the 317th Brigade, which was on my strength. In any case, I did not receive it directly from Sefer Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Can you remember how it was expressed to you? Were you simply told orally, "You have to go and see Sefer Halilovic in Jablanica on a certain date," or were you given additional information to that?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: I don't remember. I believe that it was just a short notification for me to report to Mr. Halilovic in Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Now, you've indicated that you spoke to the 3rd Corps command about your involvement in this operation. And what I wanted to ask you is: Did you speak to the 3rd Corps commander, Enver Hadzihasanovic, prior to going down to Jablanica or did you do so after you'd been to Jablanica and you knew a little bit more about what Mr. Halilovic had in mind? In other words, at what point was it that you first spoke to the 3rd Corps commander about this?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure that I spoke to him before I left for Jablanica, but I am sure that I reported to him about my travel to Jablanica and the outcomes of that meeting after I returned from Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Just to be quite clear about this, you were never given an order resubordinating you out of the organic structure of the 3rd Corps at any time; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And I just want to put some -- some propositions to you arising out of that. At all times you retained your -- your links and -- your links with and responsibilities to the 3rd Corps with regard to logistics, military security, investigation of crimes, if any, by your soldiers, and all matters outside of the combat activities of Neretva 93; is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, I understand that fortunately none of your soldiers committed any outrages against civilians in the period we're talking about, but you being the commander on the spot there can tell us this: If one of your soldiers had have been accused of or suspected of doing such a thing, the way you understood the structure that you operated under, that would have been investigated by the military security of the 3rd Corps; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: The brigade where such a crime might have occurred and security services of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. And as far as you could see -- I understand you weren't a member of the 6th Corps -- very well. Perhaps I'll just confirm that with you. You were not a member of the 6th Corps and nor were you subordinate in any way to the 6th Corps at that time; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: But as far as you could observe from the orders given by -- orders and instructions given by Sefer Halilovic in your presence, there was no resubordination of 6th Corps units but, rather, they were given tasks in the same way that you were; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: So bearing in mind the military principles that you're familiar with, had there been an offence committed by 6th Corps soldiers, that should have been investigated by the brigade and ultimately the 6th Corps military security; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Now, at the initial meeting that you had with Sefer -- sorry, now, I have a question for you about the war diary and the date of your meeting with -- the date of your first meeting with Sefer Halilovic. The war diary suggests that it's the -- the 3rd or the 4th. What I want to ask you is this: You're pretty sure that the -- the Dobro Polje meeting took place more than one day after this -- this first meeting; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: If the journalist Sefko Hodzic should -- well, I'm not sure if that's the proper way to put this question. According to your memory, it's quite possible that that meeting -- I mean, forget about the 3rd Corps diary for a minute. But according to your memory, you'd say it's quite possible that that meeting took place a bit earlier than the 3rd or 4th of September but, in fact, might have taken place on the 1st of September. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: It is possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. What you can certainly recall is that Sefko Hodzic was present on that occasion.

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Yes, he was present at our first meeting in Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Do you remember whether Sefer Halilovic had with him on that occasion an escort by the name of Sele Halilovic, S-e-l-e Halilovic?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Do you remember whether he also had with him on that occasion or the other occasion, indeed, a driver who went by the nickname of Mesar, the butcher, but his real name was Casovic?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: That's okay. But of the staff of Sefer, the personal staff of Sefer, I mean, you can remember Sele Halilovic, you don't recall Casovic. Do you recall his son, Semir, being there?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: He was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And to your understanding, he had Semir there with him because by some misfortune Sefer Halilovic's wife was blown up in her own apartment that she shared with Sefer Halilovic a month or so before; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Yes, and if I remember it well, I believe that Mr. Halilovic even said it on one occasion, that his son was much safer with him and that he would overcome the difficulties of the time better with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. Now, as you've indicated, nothing of substance was discussed when you met with Sefer Halilovic in -- in Jablanica in the company of Zuka but that it was when you got into the car with Sefer after that and drove to the village near Konjic that he explained to you what was being contemplated; is that true?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. It's a bit deceptive looking at the road maps nowadays. How long did it take on that occasion to get from Jablanica up to Konjic?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: I don't think that the Jablanica-to-Konjic journey lasted long. But from Privor, where I could use the vehicle, up to the arrival at my destination, it might have taken some four or five hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: We've had some evidence from Mr. Gusic that the Jablanica-to-Konjic road had its difficulties. On this occasion when you drove there, was the road open? I'm talking about your journey with Sefer Halilovic on this particular evening.

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, in any event, you can recall meeting with Salko Gusic at this village. Can you indicate at that time whether Mr. Gusic had any staff members with him?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: I don't remember. I believe there was an escort with him and that at this depot where we met there were some logistics staff there, but I don't remember that any staff members were there with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: But one thing's quite clear: The purpose was -- the purpose expressed by Sefer Halilovic in bringing about this meeting was that you were going to have to work with Mr. Gusic because his 6th Corps -- he and his 6th Corps were going to be involved in this operation; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And, in fact, just to jump forward to something else so that there's no doubt in this court as to the truth: When you did have the meeting at Dobro Polje later on, Salko Gusic was there; correct?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: That map was displayed on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Yes, I believe that was the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. It had -- yes. Okay. And on that occasion, Mr. Gusic was -- was included in the discussions and played his part in assigning the tasks to units from the 6th Corps; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And to your knowledge, Salko Gusic remained involved in the operation as commander of the 6th Corps as long as it lasted; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: That was my understanding.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And from the date of the 5th of September at Dobro Polje, when that map was displayed, the name written on the map, "Operation Neretva," was known to those involved in it; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Now, I just want to take a step back to the short -- the shorter meeting that you had early in -- in September. After that meeting was completed -- perhaps I should ask you this: At that meeting, did Sefer Halilovic show you or tell you about this order from the 30th of August signed by Rasim Delic creating an inspection team?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: I don't remember him mentioning this. If I believe well, he told me that he was there on the ground with a number of people from the General Staff to coordinate combat activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And you've used the term "coordinate" there. Is that -- is the Bosnian term appropriate to be used there, the term "rukovodjenje," which I've probably mangled in pronunciation, but the term "rukovodjenje"?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Control, "rukovodjenje"; and coordination, "koordinacija" are somewhat different terms.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. But under the heading "rukovodjenje" one of the functions that's performed is the function of coordination, "koordinacija"; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: In principle, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. And the system -- there is a system in the army referred to as RIK, which is "rukovodjenje i komandomenje"; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: What's the connotation of those two terms, "rukovodjenje" on the one hand and "komandomenje", on the other hand?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: The term "rukovodjenje" implied the function of control of general character in the social institutions, including the army. It was a generic term and as such it was above the term of "command." The command as a function was specifically related to the military organisation --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: -- and involved a more formal and firm approach to the organisational units that were under that term, or rather, to the entire function that it was supposed to perform. In practice, also in the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, this term RIK, was a syntagm that was often used.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. And I'm going to ask you some questions from particular manuals at a time just in the future.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: But could the witness please be shown now the order of the 30th of the 8th. Your Honour, I had marked to show MFI146 but I don't want that one shown because we've agreed now on a later version, and I just don't have the number, I'm sorry to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, could I just ask: The -- the subsequent order that -- where there's been a -- when this Court submitted that document for a further review, has that been put into evidence yet formally or not? I -- I don't have a note of it being done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. I think according to my record, it's 150. But sometimes we used the number 146. But whatever we are going to use it, we'll refer it to the August 30th order.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Just so that the witness -- the witness needs to have the order -- there's no controversy about the Bosnian order. It's all an English controversy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, perhaps if we could -- if the witness could be shown MFI146, the Bosnian version, and those English speakers in the court can bear in mind the -- the other issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Do you have in front of you the Bosnian version of the order of the 30th of August?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, you'll see that that order -- there's a preamble to the order. Could I just ask you to indicate what's the significance of that preamble.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I wonder if I could have the English version. At the moment I've got the Bosnian version.

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: To me this means that the order constitutes an implementation of the conclusions adopted at the meeting of the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did you -- do you -- are you in a position to comment whether that is an adoption of the conclusions of the General Staff at the Zenica meeting, or not?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it's an implementation of these conclusions. Could you please have the preamble on the screen again.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could that be provided to the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: This order aims at removing the shortcomings that were mentioned in the conclusions of the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. And I'm really talking -- what I'm asking you now about is the limits that this -- the limits on the inspection team which are imposed by this order, and in particular the limits imposed on Sefer Halilovic by this order. First of all, in the preamble, is the -- the competence of this team limited to the zones of responsibility of the 4th and 6th Corps, in specific terms in the last line of that preamble?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. And is that picked up -- is that picked up again in the first line of paragraph 1, indicating that "The task is to coordinate -- is to form a professional inspection team to coordinate the work and tasks in the zone of responsibility of the 4th and 6th Corps." And therefore what I'm asking you about here is: Is the competence of this team effectively limited to the 4th and 6th Corps by the terms of the order?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Yes, based on the order, that would be my conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Now, the instruction given appears to be there: Professional inspection team to coordinate. Now, that part of paragraph 1 does not place the team leader of this inspection team under the command of the 4th and 6th Corps under any circumstances, does it?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I want to move now to the tasks that are assigned, and -- just excuse me a moment. Sorry. If you'd just look at those tasks. There are four tasks as -- the main tasks that are listed in paragraph 1. And what I want to ask you about them is this: Those tasks have to be read in light of the preamble and the first sentence in paragraph 1; is that correct? In other words, in interpreting the powers given to this inspection team and its leader in those four points, you as a soldier interpreting this -- this order would of course have regard to the preamble and the first sentence in paragraph 1 in order to interpret the ambit of those powers; is that true?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Now, next of all, those -- sorry if you'd just look at paragraph 2 now. You'd see that the office given to Sefer Halilovic is the office of team leader. Now, you as an experience military person would agree that if this order was designed to appoint Sefer Halilovic as a commander of an operation, it would say that; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And -- yes, thank you. Look at paragraph number 3 now, and in particular I want you to look on the second line of paragraph 3. That's the bit I'm going to stress. But I'll read the whole thing: "The Chief of Staff of the SVK of the armed forces should, in keeping with his authority, solve the problems in the field by issuing orders." Now, does that paragraph appear to you to give the team leader a limited and confined power to issue certain orders?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And does it give that power with two important limits imposed upon it? First of all, that those orders have to be issued - and I quote now - "In keeping with his authority"? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Whose authority? I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. No, sorry, well, don't be misled by me. But just have regard to the actual paragraph itself. Look at the first sentence again. Do you see the phrase there "in keeping with his authority"? That's how it's translated in English. It comes after the -- after the term: "The Chief of Staff of the SVK --"

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Do you have that now?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I don't know whether in Bosnian it comes out more as "consistent with his authority," or "in keeping with his authority" but do you see is that phrase there in front of you?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. So do you agree with me that that phrase imposes a limit on the type of orders that -- that the team leader, Sefer Halilovic, is empowered to issue?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Yes. I understand that the authority or powers are those as defined under item 1; whereas, for any instances where this authority has not been provided for, the commander should be consulted.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. And in -- in saying what you just said there, you're, I take it, picking up that requirement to consult with -- the requirement in the last sentence of that paragraph.

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. And the other limit that's imposed upon the power given to the team leader, Sefer Halilovic, in paragraph 3 is that "Such power can be exercised with the purpose to solve the problems in the field." Now, do you see that phrase -- the phrase "solve the problems in the field"?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: [No audible response]

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. Now, do you agree with -- sorry, again, you nodded your head there but there was no audible response. Did you agree with my -- the proposition I put to you?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you. Very well. Now, under no circumstances can this order here be regarded as an order appointing Sefer Halilovic commander of any unit and of any operation; do you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: I do agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Now, I move on now to the time after -- I'm sorry, I'm...?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Maybe you could take a break at this time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I saw you are leaving that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, I am living it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We'll resume at quarter to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, could I just indicate for the convenience of all parties, I think it's likely that this witness will go over to tomorrow and I think probably by about half an hour. You can see there's -- it's a methodical way to go through things. It's not likely we'd finish him today. It is likely that we'd finish him in the early part of tomorrow. And I say that because the Prosecutor has to organise witnesses. So that's how I think it will proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, please continue, Mr. Morrissey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Cikotic. On the screen still appears that order, and I have one final question concerning that order, or one final topic concerning that order. Do you have that order still on your screen, Mr. Cikotic?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Would you look, please, at -- at paragraph 4. There's -- paragraph 4 in English here is rendered "the monitoring should begin on 31st August," but in B/C/S the word that is used there is the word "kontrola"; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. Now, we referred earlier to the system of command and control -- the system of RIK, R-I-K, rukovodjenje and komondovanje. Under the heading of "rukovodjenje" are various other more specific functions. Is one of those functions the function of kontrola?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And is one of the other functions a distinct function, the function of command, komandi?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: So paragraph 4 specifically refers to: "The kontrola should begin on 31st August and be completed by" a -- unspecified date at the bottom of the page; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And in other words, both at the start of this order and at its very end the real true functions of this -- of this inspection team are made absolutely explicit; correct?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Yes. That's what one can conclude on the basis of these documents here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I'm going to in a moment go to some military theory that may be of importance to the Tribunal at a later time. I just have one narrative matter I want to deal with before that. This order being issued on the 30th of August, you then met with Sefer Halilovic and Zulfikar Alispago in Donja Jablanica on a date early in September and you then went back to your area of responsibilities in the zone of the 3rd Corps; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And at that time, you discussed with your commanding officer, Enver Hadzihasanovic, what -- whether or not you were indeed permitted and authorised to be a part of this operation and Hadzihasanovic gave you the -- the right -- sorry, gave you permission to go ahead; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: We didn't talk. I sent him a written report where I asked for his approval for me to go ahead with the activities, and I did receive one.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I understand. In the -- I'm going to ask you about your -- your request in a minute. But in the reply that you received from Hadzihasanovic, did he go into detail as to why he was giving you that approval, or did he just give you a functional military answer, "Yes, you have approval"?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: I don't remember the contents of this communication of ours, but I don't think that there was any specific approval.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I understand. It's the fact you needed to speak to -- to your commander, Hadzihasanovic, for two reasons: The first being that you had not been resubordinated, your unit, OG Zapad, had not been resubordinated out of the 3rd Corps; and secondly, to your knowledge Halilovic was the Chief of Staff of the Supreme Command Staff rather than the commander of the Supreme Command Staff. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: It is true that I continued being within the 3rd Corps, but had the commander of the Main Staff called upon me for any reason, I would have had to inform my superior thereof.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: If you had have been resubordinated out of the 3rd Corps, then you would not need to have contacted him; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: You mean with the commander of the 3rd Corps?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. We're now -- I'm now going to ask you some questions in an area that may be difficult for the layperson but is -- is of some significance, and these are questions about the doctrine of command and control. And as I say, they may be relevant to the Court in some time considering that -- the matters that they have to try.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I ask that the witness now be shown a textbook, and perhaps if this could be shown first to the Prosecutor. Your Honours, this is a -- this document here is a document called "Introduction to the theory of military control." It's a textbook available in libraries. We do not as yet have it copied or translated so that showing it to my learned friend now may pose its difficulties for him. But because it's a professional manual available readily to all, what I have in mind is to get the witness to look at it, to read the relevant passage, and simply to confirm that this was -- if he does confirm it, of course, to confirm that this was the applicable law and rules at the time. So that's the reason I'm doing it in the way I am. Of course I'll have to get the witness to identify the -- the document he's being shown first. That's what I have in mind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Could I just say this: I'm not sure -- it's just been basically sprung upon us. I've been handed this at the moment, as my learned friend just said. I have a recollection dim, dark, recesses of my mind that this might actually be in -- might have been an exhibit in the Strugar case. I'm fairly sure the Prosecution introduced excerpts from this particular manual, and I'm pretty sure it's been translated. It must have been over the history of the -- of the Tribunal's trials. But I -- but having not been warned of this in advance, I can't comment upon that. We would certainly want to see the English while the witness is being cross-examined. If my learned friend could perhaps delay this until the last part of his cross-examination until tomorrow morning, we might be able to find an English translation overnight, because I'm sure one exists somewhere.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. I need some flexibility from both parties.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honour, well, I'm -- look, I'm -- I agree, and I don't want the Prosecution or the Court to be disadvantaged by this. Could I indicate what I had in mind now was simply to get the witness to read it. The interpreters will then interpret it live. My learned friend would not be re-examining upon it -- redirecting today, if that's what he wants to do, of course -- today in any event. I certainly would have no objection at all, and in fact these -- these military manuals are all of their very nature tenderable. The only question is they're not much use to the Tribunal in the -- in the native language, of course. I understand that. On the other hand, the wholesale translation of military documents poses its own problems. And therefore, what I'd seek to is to proceed to ask these questions now. We can indicate that -- I've indicated before we have some translation delays which -- the registry is doing everything it can and doing the best it can. But we have got some problems, about which more can be said if you need to know. I wonder if we can be permitted to proceed with this now, just to let the witness read those thing, because the evidence is not going to be technical in nature other than the witness saying, "I agree that this was the law" or "I disagree that this was the law." So it's going to be a very simple statement of fact that we're seeking to elicit from him. Where the Prosecutor may be disadvantaged and where I want to be clear that they shouldn't be disadvantaged is that if there's some context that they are being denied, then by giving them what I'm giving them now I agree they don't have the opportunity to -- to put it in context. So if -- if we're leaving something of importance out, then of course the Prosecutor is being denied that and they should have that opportunity, I can concede that quite freely. Of course they should. But that shouldn't prevent us from proceeding now in doing what I'm going to do. It really is if the Prosecutor needs a delay or wants to point out to us something that we've done unfairly or in a way that distort it is truth, that's not the intention. I can be sure. I haven't read the -- the full thing. But we would seek to proceed now if we could.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: If we could just get the pages or the references to which Mr. Morrissey wishes to cross-examine, we might even be able to find it now while he's talking. It will be on our system.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. So in principle you do not object that we are going to proceed?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Well, I -- we are disadvantaged because -- I don't know what -- I don't know what he's going to be referring to. All I'm asking is if he could perhaps delay this part until tomorrow morning and proceed with the rest and we'll see what we can do in cooperation and find the English, which will help him and the Trial Chamber. I'm sure it's there somewhere.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I think it would be to the Prosecutor's advantage if we did it now because then they know, rather than delaying it until tomorrow, when their time is cut shorter. But I'll indicate --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, let's proceed based on this document. But, Mr. Morrissey, I have to warn you that since there is no official translations and we could only rely on the simultaneous translation, there might be some disputes, you know, concerning the translation of a certain word. I hope you don't mind. And later on if there's some official, you know, written translations, we will rely on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, it -- I thank you for that. I agree that that is an issue. But because we're dealing with official or quasi official documents, it should be that any problems like that can be sorted out sensibly at a later time without troubling the witness to come back.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: That's my hope.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Now, could I just indicate that I'm now going to put to you a document, Mr. Cikotic, from -- a book entitled "Introduction to the theory of military control," and the page I'm going to get you to look at is page 105.3. And that is noted there in the text. Now, what I'd ask you to do: Would you please read that section, that -- the noted part into the transcript, and then I'll ask you some questions about it. Would you mind reading it aloud, because then the translator will interpret it for us?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Shouldn't it be put on the ELMO so that they can actually read it from -- directly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: That's a good suggestion and I ask that that be done, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: While that's being done, would you mind just looking at the front of that book and identifying -- as the book, "The theory of military control". Are you familiar with that book?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. Are you able to see from the front cover of it -- perhaps I'll ask those formal questions in a moment. What I'll ask you to do is to read that passage. It's the encircled passage. And just if you wouldn't mind reading that so that the interpreters can interpret aloud for the rest of us.

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: "Definition of the process of control. The process of control constitutes five mutually dependent functions: Planning, organising, commanding, coordination, and control."

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I just want to ask you a question about that: First of all, do you agree that that's an accurate summary of the military principle of the process of control?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you agree that the term "rukovodjenje," as defined here, is broader than the term "command"? Is a higher-level term than the term "command"?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Do you agree also that the process of rukovodjenje is something that not only commanders take care of but is also an activity of staffs and other organs of the army?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Please repeat.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Do you agree that the process of rukovodjenje is a process that's not only exercised by commanders but also an activity that's exercised by staffs and other functionaries in the armed forces?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Yes, they do participate in it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you. Whereas, command is a function exercised pursuant to the process of single command by commanders; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you please --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown page 102 and point 2, paragraph 2 has been there encircled.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Would you please read that passage into the transcript.

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: "The military dictionary defines command as the function of control in the armed forces, with the interpretation of the right of the officers to make decisions. It is important to say that only persons authorised by law, regulations, and rules are authorised to command and not other command staffs or some other control structures."

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you. Is that an accurate quotation -- or does that quotation accurately reflect military doctrine in the Bosnian army?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Yes, I believe it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now could the witness please be shown another document. This one is uploaded. But if that document could remain there because it will be used again. Could the witness now please be shown Marked for Exhibit, MFI142. And on the B/C/S version it's page 25 of that document, but on the English version, pages 27 to 28 will need to be displayed. Yes, could I indicate while that's being uploaded that this is a Prosecution exhibit. It's the book entitled "Rukovodjenje i komondovanje." I'm sorry for the pronunciation. Very well. Thank you. Now, what needs to be shown here is page 25 of the B/C/S version. That needs to be shown to the witness on the screen.

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: I believe that I have page 28, which gives the explanation of the terms "operativity" and "confidentiality."

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. I'm sorry, you don't have the right pages as yet. You need to have page --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: The witness needs to have page 25. It may be that I misled there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, although we think the entire passage that the witness needs is on page 25 of the Bosnian version, the version Your Honours are looking at is at pages 27 and continuing into 28, so you'll need to turn over the pages in this passage.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Could I just ask you to read out, please, the section under the heading "Single authority."

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And perhaps if the Court could turn other, because the substance is on the following page in English. In Bosnian the whole thing is contained on one page. Okay. Your Honours, I think because this may be looked at by others who will give evidence at a future stage and in order to make it easier for them I shall read this into the transcript in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Mr. Cikotic, I'm going to read that into the transcript in English now, and then I'll ask you to comment. This passage is under the heading "Single authority," and it provides this: "The principle of single authority in command and control implies an inalienable right of a commander to command and control a subordinated command and a unit. In keeping with the powers deriving from the competence ascribed to a specific level of command and control. This principle ensures that in the process of command and control there is only one superior who issues commands and to whom the others report about the execution of tasks. The commander's authority is stipulated by regulations. It is his right to make decisions for which he is therefore solely responsible. In his work, a commander relies on his aides, staff, other command organs. The rights and obligations of these organs are stipulated by regulations and they are responsible for their scope of work. A commander may delegate some of his duties and obligations on the Chief of Staff, his aides, a staff organ, and subordinated commands, but he cannot delegate the responsibility for the situation in the unit and its use. The principle of single authority does not bar a commander from including a wider circle of associates into the decision-making process or from hearing out their opinions and suggestions. In that way favourable conditions are created for a commander to reach the best possible decisions and for his associates to develop inventiveness and creativity." Now, let me ask you the question: Do you agree that that accurately reflects the Bosnian army military doctrine?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Yes, because it adopted the elements of the military doctrine of the former JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Okay. Just excuse me for one moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you. Could I just ask that Mr. Cikotic be assisted again with respect to the document that's on the ELMO. And I would ask that the witness now be shown the encircled part of page 176. The correct part is now displayed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Would you please read into the transcript - and if you could read as slowly as possible, it will assist the interpreters - the encircled passage that you see on that page.

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: "The command is linked with certain formation duties; in other words, only certain places in the organisational structure are characterised by the entitlement to command."

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you. Does that accurately reflect Bosnian army doctrine?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Once again, was that inherited directly from the old JNA?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, those are the questions concerning command and control directly. I now have some questions concerning another topic that's an important topic in this case, and that is the conveying of orders, the conveying an explanation of decisions. Would you just excuse me one moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'm sorry. As with the previous document that's been shown to the witness, I now wish to show the witness another manual. It has the same -- it is in the same situation in terms of not being interpreted. It has the same shortcomings and the same difficulties for the Prosecutor, but I'd seek to follow the same proper and acknowledge again any difficulties the Prosecutor may have and indicate my preparedness to cooperate in any possible way. Could that be shown to the Prosecutor in its hard form first, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm not going to make any more comments about this, but perhaps we could be given a photocopy of the pages which have been read out and we could actually then pursue our inquiries as to whether or not it's been translated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. I think that's a reasonable request.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, frankly, I -- can I indicate that the Prosecutor are indeed being very reasonable about this. We could sort this out by having a delay of a day. It's best to proceed as best we can. But I indicate gratitude to Mr. Re for taking the approach that he does. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Mr. Cikotic -- I'm sorry, that document has just been -- the Prosecutor is just making an inquiry about that document, so I'll just wait for that to be done.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you. I've now put before the witness a document called the "Rule on the land army." Could I just ask you please, Mr. Cikotic, to look at page 77 of that document and direct your attention to point 137. Thank you. And you'll see it's marked there. Could I ask you to read slowly into the transcript the first paragraph at point 137.

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: "The conveyance of decisions to subordinates has to be timely, correct, clear, and confidential. It can be either verbal or written and it has to follow the rank of urgency and execution of certain tasks. It can be done by orders, instructions, and at command reconnaissance."

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you be able to explain perhaps in lay terms to the Tribunal here what that passage entails in practical terms? In other words, how are orders to be communicated? Before you answer that, could I just ask this: In formal terms, does that accurately state the law concerning the conveying of explanations within the Bosnian army?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: The definition of the way to convey orders was orally in a written form or by means of communication. However, this particular paragraph contains all of these elements and explains them in broader terms and also mentions the urgency, the contents of orders and commands.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: And it also mentions the relationship that exists in the conveyance of orders with regard to the subordinate units.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Would you please read -- would you please now read the second paragraph in 137 right down to the end. And if you don't mind, please read it as slowly as possible because the interpreters are simultaneously interpreting.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The interpreters could always read it themselves directly from the book. That might be quicker.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I think --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: But we only have one book there. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour. And I think the interpreters may benefit from having the -- the document on the screen as they do, but at the same time, frankly, I don't know how they do it already, and I think the slower it's done, the better.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Let's try that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: So would you please read that second paragraph into the transcript.

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: "The commander's reconnaissance is the best way to convey messages to the subordinates -- to convey orders to the subordinates. It is carried out with all the subordinates or the cooperating commanders of units or only with those who are in charge of the tasks in -- within the forthcoming mission. It is carried out by the commander and in some situations and on some axes it can also be done by the Chief of Staff. This serves to lay out and define the tasks that the units -- unit is going to have and this is done in the form of orders and also cooperation is organised. The course of the action is defined by the plan of the commander's reconnaissance."

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Could I just ask for this comment: It's one of the important roles of a Chief of Staff to convey the orders of the commander and explain them in detail to the units who have to carry them out; is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: This is accurate. What is underlined here is the function of cooperation or concert activity.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. And that function plainly fell within the role that Sefer Halilovic indicated to you when he spoke to you about the forthcoming operation early in September 1993; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: That's the way I understood it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could the witness now be shown another document. This is a third document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Morrissey, I think, you know, before we leave those two documents, we'd better have a number, you know, on these two so that they could be traceable in the future.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's certainly correct. It's likely I'll come back to them. But -- but yes, that's why I didn't give them a number now. But I agree, we'll give them a number straight away. Could the -- the first of those documents -- would you just excuse me a moment, please. The first document entitled "Introduction to the theory of military control," we would ask be marked for Exhibit -- as MFI195; the second of those documents, which was the "Rule on the land army" I would ask --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Sorry, "Rule on divisions of the land army." I apologise. It should be marked MFI196.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Now, the next document to be -- I'd ask that the witness look at, please, is the "Rule on the corps." This document suffers from the same shortcomings as the previous two. I offer it as MFI197. And I note for the record that this is not the original book but a photocopy of it and should evidence need to be called about how it -- how it came to be, we're happy to oblige. It may be that the Prosecutor can have a chance to review that first and, if satisfied of the bona fides of it, they may not require that of us and they can raise any questions with us, but at this stage I offer it as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, with respect to that rule on the corps, would you please turn to page 50, point 105, and look at paragraph number 1. And now, would you please slowly read into the transcript the -- the heading next to "105", and the paragraph immediately below it.

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: "A decision is conveyed to the subordinate commands as soon as it is made, taking into account the urgency to convey this order as soon as possible to their end executives. "If the time other conditions so allow, the subordinate commander wills be present during the decision-making process. If due to distances and other reasons this cannot be provided for, the decision will be conveyed to the subordinates in written form or orally during the commander's reconnaissance, via combat orders, commands, and similar."

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: "The commander will decide on the ways decision is going to be conveyed, and the conveyance of the decision will be in the hands of the Chief of Staff. He will organise it."

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I have a question about that last sentence. It's clear that according to this rule the commander decides how his order is to be conveyed and the delivery of that order and its communication is in the hands of the Chief of Staff. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, I wish to show the witness another document. This one is the textbook, "Rukovodjenje i komondovanje." Would Your Honour just excuse me. Mr. Cikotic, just excuse me a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: And what's the number for that document you just used?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: The previous document should be marked as MFI197. The current document I'm going to show is a Prosecution document and is currently MFI142. But, however, the passage that I want to show to the witness has not yet been interpreted into English, so that even though it has an existing exhibit number, because it hasn't been interpreted it may be appropriate to give it a further exhibit number because the passage that is now being put is different, and so that people can work backwards and work out what has been shown, I will be offering this as MFI198.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I don't agree with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It may well have been interpreted into English at one point. If I can just emphasise that if my friend is going the put public documents to the witness as before, it would certainly assist everyone if he told us and we would be able to check our own records see if it has been interpreted. That isn't really revealing his hand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, that depends on the willingness from the Defence team, you know --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: -- because sometimes the cross-examination is quite unpredictable.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Well, Your Honour, could I just put on record something about that. The Prosecutor is right to feel caught out in a sense. I fully appreciate that. But it's -- it's not tactically clever to conceal public documents like this. Sometimes you do hold things back in order to surprise. Not when it's of this nature. This is simply being done as quickly as we -- as we can. There'll be other times when certainly we will be keeping things in our hand. This isn't a time when we're doing that deliberately. I do acknowledge the Prosecution's situation. Nevertheless, that having been said, I'd now seek to press on. I just ask that the witness be shown the textbook "Rukovodjenje i komondovanje." This would be offered as MFI199. Now, could the witness please be shown, first of all, page 338 on the ELMO, and there is a sentence in yellow brackets there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Would you please read that sentence in the yellow brackets three lines from the top into the transcript.

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: "When the commander words a decision and defines all of its elements, it gives it a legal force that all the subordinates have to abide by. However, the wording of the decision in the form of a document in addition to everything aforementioned also provides for the following: Giving combat orders to the subordinate units, a suitable way to inform the superior officer, and the implementation of control, and the implementation of tasks which have been given to the subordinates."

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Cikotic. Does that accurately state the -- the military rules of the Bosnian army?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Would you please look on the opposite page - that's 339 - there's a section there under the heading of "Informing of a decision," encircled in orange. Would you please read slowly that passage into the transcript.

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: "A decision taken by a commander shall become the basis for command over units and shall become a binding document only once it has been conveyed to those who will implement it. The significance and importance of the conveyance of the decision lies in the fact that subordinate units cannot carry out any combat activities until such time as the decision has been conveyed or, rather, until such time as they have received specific tasks contained in the decision by the commander."

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And could we please move down that page now to a spot lower, which is also encircled in orange.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And would you please read that lower passage on page 339 into the transcript.

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: "The decision taken by a unit commander on a case-to-case basis may be conveyed to those who will implement it in one of the following ways: Verbally, on the ground, through commander's reconnaissance on the ground, or by issuing commands; in writing, in a command, or brief orders; on the map; over communications means; in front of the lined-up units verbally (exceptionally only when it is necessary to explain the significance and the objective of the forthcoming combat)."

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you. And applying that to the concrete case here, Sefer Halilovic as Chief of Staff did indeed relay the orders and the tasks pursuant to the bigger order on that map to the subordinate commanders at Dobro Polje; do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And now having regard to that map that's next to you. If you wouldn't mind just having a look at that. Were the orders that -- that Sefer Halilovic conveyed to the commanders at Dobro Polje all completely consistent with what is depicted on that map so far as you're able to remember it?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC
utterances.text: Yes, to the extent I remember, especially in the part that concerned my task.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Cikotic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: That can now be removed from the ELMO. I have now completed that part of the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Well, would you please inform us about the number of that part from the document 142.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: That was -- those three sections were pages 338 and then two sections from pages 339. This document, as I indicated, has only been partially translated, so up to page 89 it does -- as I say, the Prosecutor may well have a translation of it somewhere in the archives.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: But let's have a separate MFI number on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Does Your Honour wish for a separate MFI number for each of those passages or just for the book?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: No, for -- for those passages.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: For each passage?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: It might be 198.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could the passage from page 338 be marked as MFI198; the first passage on page 399 be marked as MFI199; and the final passage be marked as MFI200. I have, Your Honours, two more questions relevant to that and then I understand that there's a matter that has to be raised. And the next topic is -- is a substantive one, so perhaps if I ask those two topics and then complete the -- if -- if Your Honours wish to raise another matter before close.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think we still have eight minutes, but I'm not sure that we could finish our sitting this morning, so we'd better, you know, stop here for the cross-examination and continue tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: As Your Honour pleases.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, witness, thank you very much for coming here to give your evidence. I'm afraid that you have to stay here overnight and during this period you are still under the oath, so as I did to other witnesses, do not talk to anybody and do not let anybody talk to you about your testimony. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Madam Usher will show you out of the room. We'll see you tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour. Good afternoon. The Defence would like to raise a matter which relates to the next witness in this case, Mr. Jasarevic. The Defence has received yesterday an indication as to the exhibits which the Prosecution was proposing to use in relation to that witness. Among the exhibits -- the list of exhibits which the -- which the Prosecution has put forward, there are, I believe, 20 new exhibits, that is, the exhibits which Your Honour have granted leave to the Prosecution to add to its list on the 14th of February. In the disposition to that decision - this is number 3 of the order - the Trial Chamber stated or ordered the Prosecution, and I quote, "To introduce the new exhibits at a later stage in the proceedings in order to provide the Defence with adequate time to examine them." The Trial Chamber will remember that on previous occasions the Defence has refrained from objecting to the use of a number of exhibits which were not yet on the Rule 65 ter exhibit list of the Prosecution with a view to speed up proceedings and not to block those proceedings. On that -- on this occasion, however, the Defence strongly objects to all of those exhibits being used at this stage. And as I mentioned earlier, there are 20 of them. The basis for that is essentially the one that was mentioned by Your Honour in our own decision, which is the necessity for the Defence to have adequate time to acquaint itself with those to prepare them and also to discuss it with our client, Mr. Halilovic. We'd therefore like the Trial Chamber -- we pray the Trial Chamber to enforce that part of its decision of the 14th of February and to not permit the Prosecution to use any of those 20 proposed exhibits tomorrow in relation to that particular witness. If the Trial Chamber would not -- were not minded to do so, the Defence might have to ask for additional time, again as provided in your decision of the 14th, in order to prepare for those exhibits and discuss them with Mr. Halilovic. The Defence wants to make it clear on that point that we do not wish to postpone the testimony of Mr. Jasarevic and that other than for those exhibits, the ready -- the Defence is ready to go ahead with the cross-examination. So we would skimpily -- simply ask the Trial Chamber to enforce the decision of the 14th of February on that matter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And I believe that we have been already furnished with exhibit list by the Prosecution. And, Mr. Mettraux, would you please be more specific concerning which documents belong to the category you mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely, Your Honour. I believe that this is the last 20 exhibits on the list. That would be exhibit from number 150 to 170. I will be corrected by the Prosecution if I have made a mistake in that regard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Your Honour, this matter should have been brought up at the last break between counsel. We've had no notice that this matter was going to be raised. No one has notified me or any member of this team. With regard to those documents, if -- if this matter was raised, we could have talked, possibly worked it out. We just went through a whole hour of being -- of having documents introduced that we had never seen. There were no translations here. We could have discussed it, seen what time they need, if they need time. All of these documents have been supplied to them, the translations to these, between the 4th and the 15th of February. So at the worst, they've had at least eight days to review the documents. If it's a matter of additional time is needed, we can finish this witness today, the next witness, and possibly resume on Monday, if it's a matter of a few days. If it's a matter of a few hours, we can finish this witness, finish the next witness, who hopefully will be well by tomorrow, and give them the afternoon off and resume on Friday. But some of these matters, if -- if we had more cooperation here, can just be worked out among the parties and know that these issues are being raised and we can just both approach the Court or the legal officer. These are all ABiH documents. They have people who are non-B/C/S speaking on their team. They have their non- -- they have their military advise sitting right here. They've had enough time to take care of this. And we'd ask that if there's additional time that they need, if it's a day or so or a few hours, please let us know. We can put the witness off from tomorrow till Friday or Monday, if necessary. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I agree with you on this aspect, that the parties should meet to discuss all those matters. Only as the last result it could come to our help.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes. Just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: And -- and, Mr. Mettraux, I believe that the Prosecution made a proposal to you. What's your response to that?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, just to -- just to respond to the issue of forewarning the Prosecution. We were just as surprised as they were to see those documents being put forth in relation to that witness, considering that a week or so ago the Chamber had made a clear ruling in relation to those documents. As we indicated, we have prepared ourself for the cross-examination of that witness on the basis that Your Honours' order of the 14th of February would be complied with; namely, that those documents would not be used. The Defence has spent a lot of time in the last week preparing the current witnesses and the witness that is to appear tomorrow with the documents in -- with the documents already on the exhibit list in mind and not those new documents. So the Defence team is only human and it's been an enormous task this week to prepare for those documents. So with a view to continuing with the proceedings and not delaying further, we would propose simply to go ahead with that witness with the documents which are not new documents and the Prosecution having to find what we believe another witness to put those documents through, as they would be expected to do under the order of the 14th of February.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I want to know whether there's a middle way between the two positions, that is, could we have this witness heard on Friday or next Monday and -- because, you know, if, you know, this witness is halfway down, we have to recall him back, you know, to this Tribunal and to ask, you know, more or less similar questions again using the new disclosure documents. And I just want to know whether we could have some flexibility, you know, on that issue. Yes. Yes, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
