utterances.text: Well, one other issue, Your Honour, is those are document which is we want and need to discuss with our client. And unfortunately, we are not allowed or permitted to go and visit Mr. Halilovic during the weekend. So that's an added problem that we face at this stage. So that would mean if this witness were to be delayed yet further, we would at least need him to be postponed until later next week to have an opportunity to discuss those documents with Mr. Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Just a few points, Your Honour. Number one, these are not voluminous documents. Number two, they've had them, again, in B/C/S for quite a long while. And I also know from the Simic case, the Bosanski Samac case, where the Court made an order or the Court through the Registry requested to the detention centre authorisation for counsel to go into the -- the jail during the evening. I think they -- they were allowed to go in on Friday evening. So with the Court's assistance, we might still be able to speed this up through the Registry to make a request, if that's what they need, to meet with their client over the weekend. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. By the way, are there any other witnesses available?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: We have the witness who has been ill. I don't want to say his name because he's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I know. I know. But --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: That's it, Your Honour, right now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Is he in a condition to testify tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I will know as soon as we get out of court. He -- he's -- the witness started on antibiotics yesterday, so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Mr. Morrissey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honour, thank you. Yes or no, in relation to that witness, I'll be dealing with him. I think it's appropriate that we speak further with the Prosecutor. We'll do that. But we want to make it quite clear that the difficulties are not simply related to the time lapse here. Those new documents in the main should not be tendered through this witness and we'll be making a submission to that effect. A lot of the documents are -- Mr. Jasarevic is a military security -- he's -- in fact, he was the head of military security or the chief of the SVB, as you'll hear them called throughout. Now, one of the reasons why the Prosecutor are calling Mr. Jasarevic, among various reasons, is because he may be able to say something about what Sefer Halilovic knew concerning some members or all members of the 9th Brigade. And that's a matter that the Prosecution, of course, are entitled to. They've set out to prove it, so they're of course entitled to try. That doesn't mean that they're entitled to fling any allegation that comes along through any witness that comes along. And some of these documents on their face -- and frankly, I've read the bulk of them already. As my friend say, they're not voluminous. That's not the issue. But they don't seem to have anything to do with that witness whatsoever. And I can indicate that there will be some substantive objections taken not just as matters of form but just because he's not the right person. So that -- that's unlikely to be resolved between the parties. I can say that we're not standing on ceremony here. We do wish to cooperate. It's not a -- it's not a question of delay. We don't want this witness to go. We've worked on him. And frankly, I can indicate I prepared him once before. That preparation has gone sour and I've forgotten it and now I've had to prepare him again. So it's definitely not in the Defence's interest to put him off and we don't want to. But we relied on the Court order. And as my friend indicates that, we based our -- our preparation around that. There may be other witnesses. One looks forward to hearing from Mr. Alispahic and his erstwhile employee Mr. Mujezinovic when they come and perhaps they could give evidence about these things. So I indicate there is a controversy that might be resolved simply by matters of timing and I indicate that we'll discuss it with the Prosecutor and perhaps Your Honours might suspend ruling on my friend's -- on Mr. Mettraux's -- what Mr. Mettraux has raised orally. He -- You could suspend the issue until my friends -- my learned friends from the Prosecution and I have discussed what can be done to palliate it. But adds he points out, it's not a matter of timing. There are substantive difficulties. However, we will speak about it and advise the Chamber tomorrow what the position is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, with this witness, we have now almost completed the difficult slogging through military doctrine, and there is not a great deal left. I'm not -- he's going to comment on a couple orders and he's going to give some narrative evidence and then the cross-examination is finished. It seems to me likely that the other witness, should he be well enough, should also contemplate being finished within the day tomorrow. So Mr. Jasarevic is -- is coming the following day. And therefore the matter will need to be decided tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, thank you very much. And I believe that we have already passed the time allocated to our sitting, and I hope the parties could meet together this afternoon to discuss this issue and try to find a way out on that one. I'm prepared to hear the report from the parties tomorrow morning, the first thing. So the sitting for today is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 24th day of February, 2005, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.52 p.m.,
